To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TPC-H benchmark can be efficiently implemented on many-core column-store systems by translating the query execution plan into a function performing the query and executing the resulting query plans in a single pass.

(i) a single function performing a query in one pass can outperform the state of the art by one to two orders or magnitude and (ii) a single function is simple and easy to implement, and thus, a good candidate for automatic query plan generation.

1) the TPC-H benchmark queries can be executed efficiently in one pass, 2) a single pass is achieved by translating the execution plans to functions that perform the entire query, 3) the execution of these queries in one pass can be parallelized, and 4) a many-core implementation of these functions can scale near-linearly with core counts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1. Query optimization: We present a query optimization approach for the TPC-H query workload.
the efficient implementation of complex queries on main memory databases, and we present a new, highly efficient, and easy to generate query execution plan for the TPC-H queries.

the following questions: How can decision support queries be executed efficiently on modern many-core processors? What are the main bottlenecks and how can they be overcome? What is the impact of the main memory column-store architecture on efficient query execution? How does the query plan look like for a many-core column-store?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
column-store databases are the most efficient solution for decision support workloads on main memory systems.
the TPC-H benchmark does not represent a realistic workload for a modern column-store database.
the main memory column-store approach is superior to the traditional row-store approach for decision support applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of decision support queries can be improved by orders of magnitude using modern many-core processors.
we have shown how the combination of a main memory column-store, a modern many-core processor, and a data-centric query execution model can lead to a new generation of decision support systems.
we show that the combination of main memory, many cores, and column-stores can be a very powerful platform for data-intensive decision support applications, even for complex queries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a main memory database system should strive for a high-level, declarative query interface, and the implementation should focus on efficient CPU utilization and data locality.
the performance of main memory database systems can be improved dramatically by considering the whole query and its execution plan instead of focusing on individual operators.
the performance of modern column-store databases can be significantly improved with a few well chosen architectural changes.
